faqs.q: What are the Dixon Boss hose menders used for?
faqs.a: Dixon Boss hose menders are iron or plated steel splices from 1/2" to 3" with collars that engage the gripping fingers of Boss clamps, so the hose joint is held by the Boss clamp rather than a plain screw clamp. This listing carries 8 part numbers, covering 1/2" to 3".

faqs.q: Which sizes are the Dixon Boss hose menders available in?
faqs.a: The listing carries 8 part numbers, from M1 for 1/2" to M21 for 1-1/2", within a size range of 1/2" to 3". Quote the Dixon part number or the hose size when you enquire.

faqs.q: How should I select the Dixon Boss hose menders for my application?
faqs.a: Choose the mender to match the hose bore and use Boss clamps, because the collars on the mender are shaped for the gripping fingers of a Boss clamp. A plain screw clamp will not engage them.

faqs.q: What working pressure applies to the Dixon Boss hose menders?
faqs.a: No working pressure is published for the Dixon Boss hose menders, and a mender restores flow rather than the hose's original rating, because the joint is limited by its clamps and by the hose on each side. Give us the working pressure and medium through [our contact page](/contact) and we check a figure with the maker before you order.

faqs.q: What are the Dixon Boss hose menders made from?
faqs.a: The listing gives iron, plated iron and plated steel as the materials. The plated versions resist corrosion better in damp areas; quote the part number to fix the finish.

faqs.q: Which standards apply to the Dixon Boss hose menders?
faqs.a: The listing names no ISO, SAE or EN standard and holds no certificates for the Dixon Boss hose menders. Menders are chosen by hose bore and barb size rather than by a standard. If your project needs a material or conformity certificate, say so in the enquiry and we ask the maker what it can issue.

faqs.q: Which parts do the Dixon Boss hose menders mate with?
faqs.a: The mender collars engage the gripping fingers of Boss clamps on each side of the joint. See [the Dixon hose menders](/p/dixon-hose-menders) for versions that use ordinary clamps.

faqs.q: How should the Dixon Boss hose menders be installed and maintained?
faqs.a: Cut the hose square, push each end fully over the barb of the Dixon Boss hose menders and clamp both ends with clamps sized to the hose outside diameter, then re-tighten after the first pressure cycle. A mender joins two lengths of the same hose, so check that the hose either side of the repair is sound, because it is as old as the part that failed.

faqs.q: Where are the Dixon Boss hose menders used?
faqs.a: The Dixon Boss hose menders are used to repair a cut or burst hose in the field and to join two lengths of the same hose into one run, in water, air and general-service lines where rebuilding the whole assembly would cost more than the repair.

faqs.q: How do the Dixon Boss hose menders differ from the Dixon King hose menders for 1 clamp?
faqs.a: The Boss menders have collars for Boss clamp fingers in 1/2" to 3", while [the Dixon King hose menders for 1 clamp](/p/dixon-king-hose-menders-for-1-clamp) are steel King menders designed to be held with one clamp, in 1/4" to 1-1/2". Pick the one that matches your clamps.

faqs.q: What is the Indus hose-to-hose double connector used for?
faqs.a: The Indus double connector, hose to hose, crimps onto a hose at both ends and joins two lengths into one run. It repairs a damaged section without rebuilding the whole assembly and makes up a length longer than the hose on the reel. This listing carries 10 part numbers, covering 1/4" to 2".

faqs.q: What sizes and part numbers are listed for the Indus hose-to-hose double connector?
faqs.a: The listing carries 10 sizes from -04 to -32 (1/4" to 2" hose), each its own part number such as IH-HM-DOUBLE-CONN-0404 for 1/4". Quote the Indus part number for the size you need, and tell us the hose grade and bore so we include the matching crimp ferrule.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right size or model of the Indus hose-to-hose double connector?
faqs.a: Choose the dash size to match the hose bore, then tell us the hose grade so we specify the ferrule: the ferrule follows the hose, not the fitting. A hose-to-hose connector needs a crimp at both ends, so the hose must be of a grade that crimps.

faqs.q: What working pressure applies to the Indus hose-to-hose double connector?
faqs.a: The hose grade and bore set the assembly rating, not the fitting, and a correctly crimped fitting does not derate the hose. Tell us the grade and bore on the enquiry and we confirm the figure in writing.

faqs.q: What is the Indus hose-to-hose double connector made from?
faqs.a: The connector is carbon steel, zinc-plated and Cr3+ passivated, as listed, and 316 stainless steel is available on request by adding -SS to the part number. The plating is RoHS-compliant.

faqs.q: Which standards and documents apply to the Indus hose-to-hose double connector?

faqs.q: Which parts does the Indus hose-to-hose double connector mate with?
faqs.a: The connector takes a crimped hose at each end, with a ferrule that follows the hose grade. See [the single end double connector](/p/double-connector-single-end) for the one-sided version.

faqs.q: How do I fit and look after the Indus hose-to-hose double connector?
faqs.a: Cut the hose square, push each end fully over the barb of the Indus hose-to-hose double connector and clamp both ends with clamps sized to the hose outside diameter, then re-tighten after the first pressure cycle. A mender joins two lengths of the same hose, so check that the hose either side of the repair is sound, because it is as old as the part that failed.

faqs.q: Which industries and jobs use the Indus hose-to-hose double connector?
faqs.a: The Indus hose-to-hose double connector is used to repair a cut or burst hose in the field and to join two lengths of the same hose into one run, in water, air and general-service lines where rebuilding the whole assembly would cost more than the repair.

faqs.q: How does the Indus hose-to-hose double connector differ from the Indus single-end double connector?
faqs.a: The hose-to-hose connector crimps a hose at both ends and runs from 73 mm long at -04, while [the Indus single-end double connector](/p/double-connector-single-end) is the single-ended body of the same family. Use the hose-to-hose version to join two hoses.

faqs.q: What country of origin and HS code apply to the Indus hose-to-hose double connector?
faqs.a: We ship the Indus hose-to-hose double connector from our Dubai, UAE warehouse to buyers in the GCC, Africa, Asia and beyond. The country of origin depends on the plant that made the batch and is stated on the commercial invoice. Export documents come with the order; ask on [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.a: Yes, we hold the Indus hose-to-hose double connector in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times. Request pricing for your part numbers through [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: What is the Indus single-end double connector used for?
faqs.a: The Indus double connector, single end, is the single-ended body of the same connector family as the hose-to-hose version. It crimps onto one hose, in sizes -04 to -32 with a straight configuration. This listing carries 10 part numbers, covering 1/4" to 2".

faqs.q: Which sizes is the Indus single-end double connector available in?
faqs.a: The listing carries 10 sizes from -04 to -32 (1/4" to 2" hose), each its own part number such as IH-HM-SINGLE-CONN-04. Quote the Indus part number for the size you need, and tell us the hose grade and bore so we include the matching crimp ferrule.

faqs.q: How should I select the Indus single-end double connector for my application?
faqs.a: Choose the dash size to match the hose bore, then tell us the hose grade so we specify the ferrule: the ferrule follows the hose, not the fitting. If you need to join two hoses, use the hose-to-hose connector.

faqs.q: What pressure rating does the Indus single-end double connector have?
faqs.a: The hose grade and bore set the assembly rating, not the fitting, and a correctly crimped fitting does not derate the hose. Tell us the grade and bore on the enquiry and we confirm the figure in writing.

faqs.q: What is the Indus single-end double connector made from?
faqs.a: The connector is carbon steel, zinc-plated and Cr3+ passivated, as listed, and 316 stainless steel is available on request by adding -SS to the part number. The plating is RoHS-compliant.

faqs.q: Which standards and documents apply to the Indus single-end double connector?
faqs.a: The listing gives the zinc-plated, Cr3+ passivated finish as RoHS-compliant but names no SAE or ISO fitting standard and no certificates. Indus crimps, pressure-tests and certifies assemblies in Dubai, so ask us for the test record when you order the assembly.

faqs.q: Which parts does the Indus single-end double connector mate with?
faqs.a: The connector takes one crimped hose, with a ferrule that follows the hose grade. See [the hose-to-hose connector](/p/double-connector-hose-to-hose) for the version that joins two hoses.

faqs.q: How should the Indus single-end double connector be installed and maintained?
faqs.a: Cut the hose square, push each end fully over the barb of the Indus single-end double connector and clamp both ends with clamps sized to the hose outside diameter, then re-tighten after the first pressure cycle. A mender joins two lengths of the same hose, so check that the hose either side of the repair is sound, because it is as old as the part that failed.

faqs.q: What are the brass hose menders used for?
faqs.a: Brass hose menders join two lengths of the same hose after a cut or a burst, with a barbed tail at each end held by a clamp. The listing runs from 1/8" to 3/4" in eight sizes. This listing carries 8 part numbers, covering 1/8" to 3/4".

faqs.q: Which sizes are the brass hose menders available in?
faqs.a: The listing carries 8 part numbers, one for each hose bore: 1/8", 3/16", 1/4", 5/16", 3/8", 1/2", 5/8" and 3/4". The maker's own numbers run HM-2 to HM-12, and the Indus part number is in the size table.

faqs.q: How should I select the brass hose menders for my application?
faqs.a: Match the mender to the hose bore, not the outside diameter: a 3/8" mender goes into 3/8" hose. If the hose is heavy-walled, check that the barb still fits before you clamp.

faqs.q: What working pressure applies to the brass hose menders?
faqs.a: No working pressure is published for the brass hose menders, and a mender restores flow rather than the hose's original rating, because the joint is limited by its clamps and by the hose on each side. Give us the working pressure and medium through [our contact page](/contact) and we check a figure with the maker before you order.

faqs.q: Which materials are the brass hose menders offered in?
faqs.a: The menders are brass, as listed by the maker. Brass resists corrosion in water and air lines but is not suited to every fluid, so tell us the medium if it is not water or compressed air.

faqs.q: Which standards apply to the brass hose menders?
faqs.a: The listing names no ISO, SAE or EN standard and holds no certificates for the brass hose menders. Menders are chosen by hose bore and barb size rather than by a standard. If your project needs a material or conformity certificate, say so in the enquiry and we ask the maker what it can issue.

faqs.q: What do the brass hose menders connect to?
faqs.a: Each end is a hose barb, so the mender joins two hoses of the same bore with a clamp over each barb. See [the Dixon hose menders](/p/dixon-hose-menders) for zinc-plated steel and larger sizes.

faqs.q: How do I fit and look after the brass hose menders?
faqs.a: Cut the hose square, push each end fully over the barb of the brass hose menders and clamp both ends with clamps sized to the hose outside diameter, then re-tighten after the first pressure cycle. A mender joins two lengths of the same hose, so check that the hose either side of the repair is sound, because it is as old as the part that failed.

faqs.q: Which industries and jobs use the brass hose menders?
faqs.a: The brass hose menders are used to repair a cut or burst hose in the field and to join two lengths of the same hose into one run, in water, air and general-service lines where rebuilding the whole assembly would cost more than the repair.

faqs.q: How do the brass hose menders differ from the Dixon hose menders?
faqs.a: The brass menders cover 1/8" to 3/4" in eight sizes, while [the Dixon hose menders](/p/dixon-hose-menders) reach much larger sizes and include steel and polymer versions. Choose brass for small bores in water and air; choose the Dixon range for larger bores.
